# Deep Work Plan - Full Site Description

> Spec-first, loop-closed: the repository is the harness and the plan runs itself to done.

Deep Work Plan (DWP) is an open, MIT-licensed methodology and reference kit built on four pillars: the repository is the harness; spec-first per work episode, with the plan written before code and acceptance criteria; Loop engineering, with an optional human-started daemon that prompts progress within recorded authority and gates; and measured efficiency. DWP measures the instruction bytes each flow loads. It has not shown a general saving in provider tokens. It is tool-agnostic, repo-native, and maintained by Dailybot with the open-source community.

## What Deep Work Plan Is

Deep Work Plan turns any repository into an AI-first, agent-pilotable codebase through spec-first planning, a repository-native harness, Loop engineering, and measured efficiency. It defines how to turn a goal into an agreed plan, decompose it into atomic and independently verifiable tasks, and run each task through an explicit validation gate. The methodology and kit install into the repository (AGENTS.md, docs, the .agents/ skills home, and the DWP skill) so any agent can pilot the repository.

DWP is deliberately agnostic about which AI agent or stack you use. Adapters translate the same core loop to Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, GitHub Copilot, Gemini CLI, Antigravity, Windsurf, Cline, OpenCode, and more (Claude Code and Codex are behavior-tested; the other adapters are install-tested). Plans are working state under git-ignored `.dwp/`, exportable when needed; tasks and records remain readable and reviewable. There is no runtime and no lock-in.

The methodology works alone; addons only amplify it.

## When to use Deep Work Plan

Reach for DWP when the job is:

- Making a repository AI-first: installing the agent scaffolding (context, skills, guardrails) so any coding agent can pilot it. Start with the [adoption prompt](https://deepworkplan.com/init.md) — a self-contained prompt an agent can execute directly.
- Long-horizon agent work: features, refactors, or migrations too large for one prompt, decomposed into atomic tasks that each end in an explicit validation gate and survive across sessions (resumable state on disk).
- Spec-first per work episode: write the plan before code with acceptance criteria, then execute it against validation gates.
- Handing an unfamiliar repository to an agent: the DWP documentation layer (AGENTS.md, docs/, .agents/) gives any agent the context to work safely.

Skip DWP for single-file edits, throwaway scripts, or repos an agent will touch once — the structure supports extended, multi-session work.

How an agent should engage: fetch the [adoption prompt](https://deepworkplan.com/init.md) and follow it to onboard a repository; POST JSON-RPC 2.0 to the MCP endpoint at https://deepworkplan.com/api/mcp (get_init_prompt, list_site_sections, read_page — GET is not supported, see the [MCP manifest](https://deepworkplan.com/.well-known/mcp.json)) to navigate and read this site; read the [developer portal](https://deepworkplan.com/developers) for the full API surface.

## Who Maintains It

Deep Work Plan grew out of real engineering work at Dailybot and is now maintained by Dailybot together with the open-source community.

- Dailybot: https://www.dailybot.com
- Repository: https://github.com/DailybotHQ/deepworkplan-website

## Core Principles

- Plan before execution — no code is written until the plan is agreed. The plan is a contract between you and the agent.
- Tasks are atomic — each task is scoped so it can be executed and verified on its own, then committed atomically.
- Verify everything — every task ends with an explicit validation gate before the next one begins, with progress recorded in git.
- Evidence over narrative — a task closes only on recorded evidence that satisfies its acceptance criteria; a claim, including another agent's result, stays a claim until the plan's own gate observes it.
- Delegation never lowers the bar — parallel agents work only on tasks marked safe for it, under an explicit grant, and their work is gated like anyone else's.
- Escalate only what is critical — routine decisions are made and recorded; the agent stops only for approval, consent, irreducible ambiguity, quality conflicts, damage, terms or exhausted capacity.

## Site Structure

### Pages

- [Home](https://deepworkplan.com/) — Overview of the Deep Work Plan methodology and how to get started
- [Methodology](https://deepworkplan.com/methodology) — The narrative methodology: what DWP is, its principles, the workflow, and how to adopt it
- [Specification](https://deepworkplan.com/spec) — The readable, normative DWP standard: task anatomy, validation gates, completion protocol, mandatory final tasks, archetypes, and addons
- [Kit](https://deepworkplan.com/kit) — The kit catalog: presets, adapters, and commands available for installing DWP into a repository
- [Changelog](https://deepworkplan.com/changelog) — A source-backed timeline of the releases and design decisions behind Deep Work Plan (e.g. v3's token efficiency, v4's Lite-first plans, v6's verified closure on an append-only journal, v7's delegation with evidence, swarm autonomy and Ecosystem 1.0, v8's Loop engineering)
- [Examples](https://deepworkplan.com/examples) — Worked examples that show the methodology applied to real engineering work
- [Quickstart](https://deepworkplan.com/quickstart) — A short path to getting DWP running in a repository
- [Vim](https://deepworkplan.com/kit/vim) — DeepWorkPlan Vim v1.1.0, the terminal editor for Deep Work Plan and the optional `vim` addon of Deep Work Plan v8: a generated command index (SPC h h), VS Code-shaped gestures, a read-only DWP plan browser (SPC P), a Markdown viewer (SPC m p / SPC m r), and a consent-first installer — download https://deepworkplan.com/vim/install.sh, compare its SHA-256 with the value on the page, then run `bash install.sh` (it installs its own release, v1.1.0, or the one `--version` names: an exact version, a `>=` floor or `latest`) (Neovim 0.12+, macOS/Linux, GPL-3.0).
- [Herdr addon](https://deepworkplan.com/kit/herdr) — optional v8 addon built on herdr-peers v2.2.1 (MIT): a plan with the `agent_delegation` grant hands a `parallel_safe` task to a peer agent in a Herdr pane, on any machine, and receives one authorized reply. Depth limit 1, fan-out cap 4, replies are data rather than instructions, every delegation recorded before it is relied on; the sender is not authenticated (`HERDR_PEERS_SCOPE` allow-list mitigates). Releases 1.2.0 and 1.2.1 add autopilot (`herdr-peers autopilot`): an optional daemon that only a human starts; it accepts the recommended option for agents waiting at a question, a tool approval, a plan approval, folder trust or an update prompt, never touches a login or Claude's bypass-permissions acknowledgement, never chooses a refusal or an option that widens an agent's permissions, and never keys a pane without a recognised menu. With autopilot on, an agent's request is approved without the human seeing it; there is no deny-list. Release 2.0.0 moves the wire to protocol 2 and adds: lead appointment on the human's explicit word (`lead claim --allow-appointment`; `lead takeover --as-lane`, probed twice, at most two appointments per plan; `lead verify` is the read-only check before any merge, tag or release), the autopilot brain (`--brain`: the daemon launches one dedicated agent with `ak pick --kinds` and obeys it only within a closed list of actions, fail-closed when `ak` is missing or older than 1.3.0), and the plan queue (the pack writes `.dwp/queue.json`, schema `dwp-queue-v1`; with `--loop` the daemon starts the next queued, approved plan without you). On a granted plan every lane and successor must run 2.0 or later. Release 1.3.0 adds the loop: `autopilot --loop` keeps every open plan running to its end on every machine, `--notify`/`--notify-env` point its reports where you direct them, the read-only `plans` and `fleet` verbs report state, and the fleet UI shows every lane, machine and open plan.
- [Agentkit addon](https://deepworkplan.com/kit/agentkit) — optional v8 addon built on coding-agents-kit v1.5.0 (MIT): `ak <kind> [@profile]` for claude, codex, cursor, opencode, pi, cline, grok and antigravity (plus GLM/Azure/xAI variants), profiles, headless `ak run`, `ak doctor --json`; the headless delegation transport (one `ak run` per delegate in a git worktree). Agents run in autonomy by default (the CLI's own flag, added by `ak`); the opt-out — `--ask` on one command or `AGENTKIT_PERMISSIONS=ask` — always wins, also over `--auto`. Set it on a host; a dev container is the intended sandbox. Release 1.3.0 adds pick-v2 (`ak pick --kinds` ranks across kinds, `--model-for KIND=NAME` overrides the model per kind, `--json` returns the launch contract: `launch.argv` with `launch.permissions` and a `qualifies: false` form) and makes `--model` a head flag mapped to each CLI's own flag — a behaviour change for scripts that passed `--model` through; interface 1 is unchanged.
- [Devcontainer addon](https://deepworkplan.com/kit/devcontainer) — optional v8 addon built on devcontainer-kit v1.4.2 (MIT): each repository's own dev container rendered by `dck init` (reconciled, never clobbered) — `docker/local/<service>/Dockerfile` from the official `python-3.13` / `node-24` / `debian` image pinned by digest, no shared base image — `bash dev.sh up` over the `dck` launcher, opt-in layers (coding agents through `ak`, editor, Dailybot), loopback-only binds, git over SSH through the host agent with the developer's git aliases (key files inside only on the developer's `[ssh] copy_keys` opt-in, which makes the whole host `~/.ssh` readable inside), the `dck-dockerfile` skill, and Herdr machines per container with the standard layout.
- [Compare](https://deepworkplan.com/compare) — Deep Work Plan compared with spec-driven tools, agent workflow frameworks and vendor-native plan modes: each described on its own terms, three neutral capability values, official sources, a review date and an invitation to correct
- [FAQ](https://deepworkplan.com/faq) — Frequently asked questions: what Deep Work Plan does, how validation gates and resumption work, how it differs from other tools, and how to adopt or upgrade
- [Quickstart / Adoption](https://deepworkplan.com/quickstart) — Make any repository AI-first: install the skill, onboard the repo, then plan and execute. Includes a self-contained onboarding prompt at [init.md](https://deepworkplan.com/init.md) to hand to an agent
- [Developers](https://deepworkplan.com/developers) — The agent & developer surface: a read-only, zero-auth, versioned API described by an OpenAPI spec, a stateless MCP server at /api/mcp, per-page Markdown in 17 languages, the `npx skills` install CLI, and the official `deepworkplan` CLI. Alias: /docs redirects here
- [Trust](https://deepworkplan.com/trust) — Why the skill is safe to adopt: open source, MIT, verifiable installs (SHA256SUMS), and a clear vulnerability-disclosure policy
- [About](https://deepworkplan.com/about) — What Deep Work Plan is, its core principles, and who maintains it
- [Contact](https://deepworkplan.com/contact) — How to engage with the project: source, issues, and discussions on GitHub
- [Privacy](https://deepworkplan.com/privacy) — The site's privacy policy: static site, no accounts, cookieless analytics

### DWP standard 8.0.0: v8

DWP standard 8.0.0 is the current v8 major line. New plans default to plan-contract/v8. Existing v7, v6, and v5 plans retain their recorded generation; migration happens only through an explicit `refine migrate`. v8 plans keep the plan-manifest/v7 line, and plan-manifest/v7 and journal-event/v7 remain supported for existing plans. The v8 schemas are [plan-contract/v8](https://deepworkplan.com/schema/plan-contract/v8.json), [journal-event/v8](https://deepworkplan.com/schema/journal-event/v8.json), and [plan-snapshot/v8](https://deepworkplan.com/schema/plan-snapshot/v8.json).

The four pillars are: the repository is the harness; spec-first per work episode, with the plan written before code and acceptance criteria; Loop engineering; and measured efficiency. The working sentence is: “Spec-first, loop-closed: the repository is the harness and the plan runs itself to done.” An approved plan proceeds inside its recorded authority and gates, with a human-started daemon available to prompt progress. Registration is lead claim plus succession. Nudges add no authority. Loop engineering includes failover, plan events, the fleet map, and queue starts by prompt-lead. The human is notified rather than waited on, except for logins, credentials, and the plan’s own C1–C7 gates unless pre-authorized. The daemon is optional; the methodology works alone and addons only amplify it. Governance is enforced cooperatively; it is not a sandbox. DWP measures the instruction bytes each flow loads. It has not shown a general saving in provider tokens.

### What v7 adds

Deep Work Plan v7 (pack `v7.12.2`) keeps the plan, task and gate loop and adds a verifiable record and safe parallelism:

- **A record, not a narrative.** A plan carries an immutable outcome contract and an append-only journal; a task completes only when recorded evidence satisfies its criteria. Only the plan's own gate runner mints `observed` evidence; claims stay `asserted`, and a human judgment closes a criterion only through a recorded sign-off. Spec: [record layer](https://deepworkplan.com/spec/record-layer).
- **Delegation with evidence.** A plan whose contract grants `agent_delegation` can hand `parallel_safe` tasks to other coding agents — headless in a git worktree (agentkit) or in another Herdr pane, on any machine (Herdr). A delegate's result stays a claim until the plan's gate observes it. Spec: [delegation](https://deepworkplan.com/spec/delegation).
- **Many agents, one lead.** Orchestration at scale (one lane per repository or workstream) and swarm autonomy (capacity checks at task boundaries, handoff packets before a usage limit, lead succession with epochs and fencing) keep long efforts running past one account's limit or one agent's loss.
- **Escalation only when it is critical.** Agents decide and record routine choices and stop only for seven classes: approval not granted, a consent or login screen, irreducible ambiguity, a quality conflict, damage, terms, or exhausted capacity.
- **Optional, pinned ecosystem.** Every addon is opt-in and recorded in `.dwp/config.json`; the methodology works with none. Since 7.8.0 every integrated product is stable at 1.0 under semantic versioning.

### Ecosystem (v8)

The methodology works alone; addons only amplify it. The pack 8.0.3 descriptors pin herdr-peers 2.2.0 (the site pins the v2.2.1 patch), coding-agents-kit v1.5.0, devcontainer-kit v1.4.2, deepworkplan-vim v1.1.0, Dailybot v3.23.20, and AI Diff Reviewer v3.3.16. The dependency-upgrade and design-system addons have no external pin. See the [kit index](https://deepworkplan.com/kit).
### Languages

The site ships in 17 languages. English (default) is served at the root; the other 16 live under their code: /es/, /pt/, /zh/, /ja/, /de/, /fr/, /ko/, /ru/, /it/, /tr/, /id/, /vi/, /hi/, /pl/, /uk/, /th/

Each language has its own full page set and its own Markdown mirrors.

## Content Model

- Multilingual routing: English base routes (`/`, `/methodology`, `/spec`, etc.) and 16 language routes under `/{lang}/`
- Methodology, spec, and kit content authored with Astro Content Collections supporting Markdown and MDX
- All pages use structured data (JSON-LD) for machine readability

## Topic Areas

- Structured execution for AI coding agents
- Planning and decomposing engineering work into atomic, verifiable tasks
- Validation gates and completion protocols
- Agent-agnostic workflows (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, GitHub Copilot, Gemini CLI, Antigravity, Windsurf, Cline, OpenCode, and more)
- Verifiable completion: an outcome contract, an append-only journal and gated evidence
- Delegating tasks to parallel agents with recorded, gated results
- Markdown-based, version-controlled plans and running logs
- Resumable multi-hour agent execution

## Tech Stack

- Astro (static site generator with islands architecture)
- Svelte (interactive components)
- TypeScript
- Tailwind CSS (with dark mode support)
- MDX (enhanced Markdown)
- Biome (linter and formatter)
- Deployed on Cloudflare Pages

## Agent-Friendly Markdown Endpoints

Every rendered page is available as clean, native Markdown for AI agents. This content is served directly from the original source Markdown — not converted from rendered HTML — preserving full fidelity of code blocks, links, and formatting.

### URL Patterns

- **Pages**: `/{page}.md` (EN), `/{lang}/{page}.md` for the 16 non-default languages
  - Examples: `/methodology.md`, `/spec.md`, `/kit.md`, `/init.md`, `/es/methodology.md`, `/ja/developers.md`, `/pt/privacy.md`
- **Reader entries**: `/methodology/{slug}.md`, `/spec/{slug}.md`, `/kit/{slug}.md`, `/examples/{slug}.md` (and their `/{lang}/…` variants)
- **Onboarding prompt**: `/init.md` — a self-contained prompt you can paste into an agent to make a repository AI-first

### Response Format

Each Markdown response includes:
- H1 title
- Description (blockquote)
- Metadata: Language, Canonical URL (HTML version), Last Updated
- Separator
- Original Markdown body content

Content-Type: `text/markdown; charset=utf-8`

### Content Negotiation

Agents can request Markdown without changing URLs by sending `Accept: text/markdown`:

```
curl -H "Accept: text/markdown" https://deepworkplan.com/methodology
→ Returns Markdown with Content-Type: text/markdown; charset=utf-8
→ Response includes Vary: Accept header for proper caching
```

### Why Native Markdown

- Content is served from the original source files, not HTML→Markdown conversion
- More token-efficient for AI consumption (no HTML tag residue)
- Code blocks, links, and formatting preserved exactly as authored
- Canonical URL always points to the HTML version for human readers
- Internal cross-links between pages enable agents to discover the full site structure

## Agent API

The site exposes a read-only, zero-auth agent API — no keys, no registration, declared in [auth.md](https://deepworkplan.com/auth.md):

- [OpenAPI 3.1 spec](https://deepworkplan.com/openapi.json) — every endpoint, parameter, and response schema
- [MCP server manifest](https://deepworkplan.com/.well-known/mcp.json) — describes the stateless Model Context Protocol endpoint at https://deepworkplan.com/api/mcp, served over Streamable HTTP (JSON-RPC 2.0, POST only — GET returns 405 by design, no SSE stream). Tools: `get_init_prompt`, `list_site_sections`, `read_page`. Server card: [server-card.json](https://deepworkplan.com/.well-known/mcp/server-card.json). Supports protocol versions 2025-03-26 and 2025-06-18
- [Health](https://deepworkplan.com/api/health.json) — static status marker
- [Versioned API catalog](https://deepworkplan.com/api/v1/index.json) — the `/api/v1/` family (sections, pages, health) with the site version and spec links; the unversioned canonical paths belong to the same v1 contract
- [Official CLI](https://github.com/DailybotHQ/deepworkplan-website/tree/main/cli) — `deepworkplan`: a zero-dependency command-line client over this API (`init`, `sections`, `read`, `open`, `mcp`); npm publication pending
- Versioning & rate limits — breaking changes ship only in a new `/api/v{N+1}/` family; deprecated endpoints answer with `Deprecation` and `Sunset` headers at least 180 days before removal; `/api/*` responses carry RFC 9331 `RateLimit-Limit`/`-Remaining`/`-Reset`/`-Policy` headers and `Retry-After` on 429 (best-effort, 120 requests per 60 seconds, anonymous access unchanged)
- [Developer portal](https://deepworkplan.com/developers) — quickstarts, curl examples, and the install CLI ([/docs](https://deepworkplan.com/docs) redirects there)
- **Errors**: unknown `/api/*` paths return structured JSON errors (`{"error":{"code","message","hint"}}`), never HTML; Markdown-negotiating clients that hit a 404 receive a Markdown recovery body listing the sitemap, llms.txt, and key pages

## Structured Data

The site includes JSON-LD structured data on all pages:
- WebSite schema (site-level identity)
- SoftwareApplication schema (Deep Work Plan, free, authored and published by Dailybot)
- Organization schema (Dailybot, with contact point and postal address)
- BreadcrumbList schema (navigation hierarchy)
- AboutPage and ContactPage schema where applicable
